Rachel developed a comprehensive mobile app to empower patients undergoing dialysis treatment. This app was inspired by her grandmother's health condition, and utilizes AI to bridge the gap between the patient and healthcare provider to enhance the efficiency of care.

The current residency system epitomizes government-enabled market failure. While medical school enrollments surged 33% since 2002, Medicare’s 1996 residency funding cap froze training slots—creating an artificial bottleneck where 1 in 5 applicants now face rejection. This isn’t free-market scarcity; it’s bureaucratic central planning. The 2024 data showing 8,869 unmatched graduates aligns with AAMC projections of a 124,000-physician shortage by 2035.

The Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025 directly targets such monopolistic structures by dismantling barriers to market entry. ACGME’s grip on accreditation and the MATCH algorithm’s wage suppression—protected by 2004’s antitrust exemption—distort labor markets while hospitals exploit non-compete clauses to trap underpaid residents.

Real reform requires abolishing the residency cap, expanding Medicare-funded slots via bills like the Resident Physician Shortage Reduction Act, and applying antitrust scrutiny to accreditation cartels. Without competitive pressure, DC’s Soviet-style quota system will keep rationing doctors while patients wait.
